body: In 1860, Scott de Martinville’s machine traced “Au Clair de la Lune” in soot on paper so he could look at the sound, not play it back. You can hear it at the first link: somebody figured out how to give us ears for paper.

receipts.title: First Sounds — The Phonautograms of Édouard-Léon Scott de Martinville
quote: track the wavy lines scratched on soot-covered paper as though they were standard record grooves.
Scott did not intend his phonautograms to be played back
Scott recorded the French folksong "Au Clair de la Lune" on April 9, 1860, and deposited the results with the Académie des Sciences in 1861.

receipts.title: First Sounds — Édouard-Léon Scott de Martinville
quote: inscribed airborne sounds onto paper, over time, to be studied visually.
